sections.h2: Where do Chattooga County property taxes get paid and who sets the value?
sections.html:
The Chattooga County Tax Commissioner bills and collects, but does not set values or millage rates. The Board of Tax Assessors, appointed by the county commissioner, appraises property and approves every exemption claimed. The Board of Equalization, appointed by the Grand Jury, hears appeals. The millage rate itself comes from the county commissioner for county tax and the Board of Education for school tax.

  • Tax Commissioner: Courthouse Annex, 120 Cox Street, Summerville, GA 30747; mail to P.O. Box 517, Summerville, GA 30747-0517.
  • Phone 706-857-0703. Hours run 7:30 AM to 5:30 PM Monday through Friday, and the office is closed on Wednesdays.
  • Bills can be searched and paid online at chattoogacountytax.com.
  • A mailed payment is accepted with a United States Postal Service postmark, but not with a metered postmark.

Tax bills go to the homeowner and only sometimes to the mortgage company, so forward your bill to the lender if your taxes are escrowed.

sections.h2: What is Chattooga County, Georgia like for a house seller?
sections.html:
Chattooga County in the northwest corner of Georgia was created on December 28, 1838 and takes its name from the Chattooga River. It covers 314 square miles, of which 313 are land. Summerville is the county seat, and Trion, Lyerly and Menlo are the other incorporated cities. Walker and Floyd counties lie to the north and southeast, and a corner of the Chattahoochee National Forest reaches into the county. The Summerville micropolitan area is part of the Rome-Summerville combined statistical area.

History left landmarks here. The 1863 Battle of Trion Factory was fought along present-day First Street, and the Old Trion Cemetery holds graves of soldiers killed in that fight. Several properties in the county are on the National Register of Historic Places, which matters because Georgia offers preferential assessment for qualifying historic buildings.

Two public school systems serve the county: the Chattooga County School System and the Trion City School System. Census QuickFacts estimates 25,300 residents for 2025, close to the 24,965 counted in 2020 and below the 26,015 of 2010. It lists a 2020 to 2024 median owner-occupied value of $115,600, a median gross rent of $790, a median household income of $50,285 and an owner-occupancy rate of 66.8%. Building permits for 2025 numbered 2, and the mean commute is 28.1 minutes.

sections.h2: When are Chattooga County property taxes due, and what if I am late?
sections.html:
Real estate and business personal property taxes are normally due December 1. Interest begins to accrue the day after the due date, and a penalty of 5% applies to taxes unpaid after 120 days. Homesteaded property with a tax liability under $500 does not receive that 120-day penalty. Mobile and manufactured homes are due April 1, with interest of 1% added monthly if they are late.

Unpaid taxes can be levied on, though the Tax Commissioner describes that as a last resort. After 30 days past due a tax fifa, or lien, can be recorded with the Clerk of Superior Court. These records are public and credit bureaus may pick them up, and the tax office has no control over how they use them.

Listings of excess funds from past tax sales are posted on the Tax Commissioner's website, so a former owner can check whether money is waiting.

sections.h2: Which homestead exemptions does Chattooga County offer?
sections.html:
The Tax Commissioner lists state exemptions and local ones that replace the state amount when larger. You must own and occupy the home on January 1 and apply with the Tax Assessor's Office. Applications can go in year-round but must arrive by April 1 to take effect that year, and one filed later applies the following year.

Homestead exemptions listed by the Chattooga County Tax Commissioner
ExemptionWho qualifiesWhat it does
StandardOwner who lives in the home$2,000 off the 40% assessed value; excludes bond levies
Standard elderly schoolAge 62 or older, net income at most $10,000Up to $10,000 off assessed value, school tax only
Standard elderly generalAge 65 or older, net income at most $10,000Up to $4,000 off assessed value for county, school and state
Local countyAge 70 or older, federal adjusted gross income at most $20,00020% to 100% of assessed value for county tax, primary residence and up to 5 acres
Local schoolAge 70 or older, same income limitUp to $40,000 of assessed value for school tax
FloatingAge 62 or older, household income at most $30,000State and county tax, not school; replaces other exemptions

The office cautions that the floating exemption can raise a bill at first, since it replaces other state and county exemptions already in place. Disabled veterans and surviving spouses of service members killed in armed conflict also have exemptions, as do surviving spouses of firefighters and peace officers killed in the line of duty.

sections.h2: Can Chattooga County owners defer taxes or lower the assessment?
sections.html:
Owners 62 or older with gross household income of $15,000 or less can defer, but not escape, tax on a homestead. The deferred amount generally stays due until ownership changes or the deferred taxes plus interest reach 85% of fair market value, which means a sale usually triggers repayment from proceeds.

  • Agricultural land used in bona fide farming can be assessed at 30% instead of 40%, and conservation use property is valued at its current use. Both require a covenant to keep the use for at least 10 years.
  • Qualifying historic buildings can receive preferential assessment on the structure and up to two acres around it.
  • Manufacturers can claim the Freeport exemption on raw goods, goods in process and finished goods awaiting out-of-state shipment, by applying with the Board of Tax Assessors between January 1 and April 1.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Chattooga County assessment?
sections.html:
Appeal within 45 days of the date on the assessment notice. The appeal goes first to the Board of Tax Assessors, which reviews its value again. If you stay dissatisfied, you can go to the Board of Equalization or to arbitration, and after that you may continue to Superior Court by mailing or filing a written notice with the Board of Tax Assessors.

An appeal may argue taxability, value or uniformity of the assessment compared with other properties. It may not argue that the tax is too high, because that amount is set by the county commissioner and Board of Education. Mobile home owners who disagree with a value change have 30 days to go to the Board of Equalization.

Returns are due between January 1 and April 1. After the first return, real property returns renew on their own unless something changes, while personal property returns are required each year.

sections.h2: What should I know about taxes when selling in Chattooga County?
sections.html:
Whoever holds title on January 1 owes the whole year's tax, and the Department of Revenue says Georgia has no refund for part-year owners. A closing attorney should split the year between buyer and seller on the settlement statement.

Your own exemption does not carry over to the buyer, and a buyer who plans to live in the house must apply by April 1. If you need a copy of a deed for the closing file, the Clerk of Superior Court keeps a deed room in the Chattooga County Courthouse. Because property in this county is lower priced than the other three Georgia counties compared on QuickFacts, even a modest unpaid balance and penalty can matter to a sale, so pull a payoff early.

faqs.q: When are Chattooga County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Normally December 1 for real estate and business personal property. Mobile and manufactured homes are due April 1.

faqs.q: Is the Chattooga County tax office open on Wednesdays?
faqs.a: No. The Tax Commissioner's office is closed on Wednesdays and open 7:30 AM to 5:30 PM the other weekdays.

faqs.q: What is the penalty for paying late in Chattooga County?
faqs.a: Interest starts the day after the due date. A 5% penalty applies after 120 days, except for homesteaded property with liability under $500.

faqs.q: Do I have to reapply for homestead exemption every year?
faqs.a: No. Once granted it renews automatically unless you move, change ownership or want a different exemption, and the deadline for a first application is April 1.

faqs.q: How do I find a deed copy for a Chattooga County property?
faqs.a: Ask the Clerk of Superior Court, whose deed room is in the Chattooga County Courthouse.
